name: SAP SQL Anywhere
tagline: Self-tuning embeddable SQL database with MobiLink sync, still shipped inside ISV apps but frozen at v17.
description: SQL Anywhere began as Watcom SQL and became Sybase's database for embedding inside packaged software, remote offices and mobile devices. It is notably low-maintenance: it self-tunes cache and query plans, runs with zero DBA, and its MobiLink server synchronises thousands of remote SQL Anywhere or UltraLite databases with a central Oracle, SQL Server or HANA. Version 17 dates from 2015 and SAP only ships fixes now, with mainstream maintenance extended to the end of 2028. Existing ISVs keep it because it just works; new projects should look at SQLite or PostgreSQL plus a modern sync layer.
statusNote: No new major version since 17 (2015); SAP ships fixes only and lists end of mainstream maintenance as Dec 31, 2028.

pricing.notes: Per-seat/core and OEM runtime licensing; free Developer Edition for non-production use.

scale.notes: Built for many small databases synchronised with a central server rather than one large one.

strengths: Self-tuning engine runs unattended inside shipped products with no DBA
MobiLink sync connects thousands of remote databases to a central Oracle, SQL Server or HANA
Accepts both Watcom-SQL and much of T-SQL, easing ports from ASE/SQL Server
Small footprint UltraLite edition for mobile and handheld devices
weaknesses: Frozen at version 17; no new features from SAP
Mobile SDKs and platform support lag modern iOS/Android practice
useCases: Databases embedded in packaged ISV software (e.g., PowerBuilder apps)
Field-service and retail apps that sync with HQ
Remote office databases with intermittent connectivity
notIdealFor: New mobile apps (use SQLite with a modern sync engine)
